name: blackswan-attention
description: The ATTENTION probe — the first SENTIMENT/attention stream (B3), a cheap calibration. Wikipedia daily pageviews for an asset's article (Bitcoin/Ethereum/Solana) proxy retail ATTENTION — free, no-key, per-asset, daily, mined to wiki-pageviews/<asset>.json. It asks whether an attention SURGE (pageviews in the top tail of their own past) predicts the next day's move — ride it (attention_momentum: FOMO continues) or fade it (attention_reversion: the hype day is a local top). The well-known trap is that attention tracks VOLATILITY, not direction; this measures whether any tradeable direction survives cost. Reuses the shared signal_extremes past-only core and the intraday backtest mechanics, so every existing gate/lens/scorecard reads an attention cell unchanged. The one surface new here is the pageview JOIN, which carries the publication-lag trap pinned before any number: Wikimedia publishes a day's count only AFTER that day, so a crypto bar dated D reads pageviews[D - lag_days] (lag_days>=1) — never day D's own unpublished count — making the traded return two days after the pageview day. The extreme is past-only, the position applies to the next bar, positions never read price. NOTE: sparse book, so signal_expectancy (per-trade edge net of cost) is the exposure-neutral decider alongside the gate. Deterministic and model-free (the seed is contract-only).

asset.description: Which crypto instrument's price is traded/benchmarked and whose Wikipedia article's pageviews drive the signal (BTC->Bitcoin, ETH->Ethereum, SOL->Solana). return_vs_hold_pct and capture are measured against THIS asset.

signal.description: attention_momentum RIDES an attention surge (long a top-tail pageview day, on the FOMO-continues thesis); attention_reversion FADES it (short a surge, on the hype-day-is-a-local-top thesis). A bar fires only when its lagged pageviews are at/above the attention_pct quantile (or at/below 1-this) of the PAST-ONLY distribution. An unknown value is refused.

attention_pct.description: The quantile of the TRAILING (expanding, past-only) pageview distribution at/above which the day is an attention SURGE (and at/below 1-this an attention lull). Computed only from pageviews observed at prior bars — a whole-sample quantile would be a silent lookahead. Higher demands a rarer surge.

hold_bars.description: How many daily bars a position is held after a surge, then flat. The position earns bars t+1..t+hold_bars (never the surge bar's own return), and a new surge inside the hold window is ignored.

lag_days.description: Publication lag: a bar dated D reads pageviews[D - lag_days]. lag_days=1 is the minimum safe lag (a day's count is published only after that day); larger values test robustness to slower publication / conservative timing. The traded return is (lag_days + 1) days after the pageview day.

transaction_fee.description: Per-side fee, charged on turnover at entry and again at exit (~0.2% round trip at the default). Because surges are rare the book is sparse, so realized_cost_bps is moderate — the per-trade edge is the question.

walk_forward_window.description: Which out-of-sample span is ACCOUNTED. Only the test window's daily bars enter the metrics; the month before it is a formation lookback for the past-only pageview distribution. alt-2024 (crypto BULL) and alt-2025 (crypto BEAR) are the decisive pair — a real attention-direction edge must hold in BOTH, not flip sign with the regime.

seed.description: Present for contract conformance only — the backtest is fully deterministic, so seeds are not swept (identical cells would fake replication).
